description: Stream a command's output as it runs. POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/commands with `stream: true` answers 200 application/x-ndjson, one CommandStreamFrame per line (the spec's own components.schemas.CommandStreamFrame), but the converter reads only application/json bodies, and the same route answers JSON without `stream`, so executeSandboxCommand keeps its JSON output. Add streamSandboxCommand on that route, marked server-streaming with the frames as its output's items, so it generates as API.makeStreaming: `.stream(input)` emits each frame as Boat writes it, and BoatProtocol frames the body as NDJSON. Its input requires `stream`. The frame shape is CommandStreamFrame plus the members of CommandResponse that the spec says the `exit` frame carries ("the synchronous result without stdout/stderr"). @boatdev/sdk's streamCommand reads the same stream.

traits.smithy.api#documentation: Public Sandbox id returned by create/list/get sandbox calls.
Relative working directory inside the sandbox work directory.
Command timeout in seconds. Values outside 1-600 are rejected with a 400 invalid_timeout error.
Send `true`: Boat answers with newline-delimited JSON (application/x-ndjson), one CommandStreamFrame per line. Without it the route answers one JSON body; call executeSandboxCommand for that.
started: the command's record in the command history.
stdout/stderr: the chunk of output, UTF-8.
True when the memory ceiling killed the command or one of its processes and the command failed.
error: true when the command provably never ran (the sandbox is still restoring its disk), so sending it again is safe.

One line of a streamed command (`POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/commands` with `stream: true`, application/x-ndjson).
- `started`: first line. `commandId`.
- `stdout` / `stderr`: a chunk of output in `data`.
- `exit`: last line when the command ended. The synchronous result without stdout/stderr: `success`, `exitCode`, `signal`, `oomKilled`, `timedOut`, ...
- `error`: last line on a failure. `error`, `message`, `retryable`.
Every line of the output stream, in order. It ends after an `exit` or `error` frame.

Run a command in a sandbox and stream its output

executeSandboxCommand with `stream: true`: the output arrives as the command writes it, one frame per line. `started`, then `stdout`/`stderr` chunks, and last exactly one `exit` or `error`. The 600s timeout cap applies; for a longer command, start it with `detached: true` and follow it with attachCommand. An `error` frame with `retryable: true` means the command never ran (the sandbox is still restoring its disk), so sending it again is safe.
